intervention.notes: Main approach: PartitionedMemTable routes Put() to P=16 sub-tables at write time using L1 key range boundaries. Each sub-table has independent 4MB budget (64MB/16). When a sub-table fills its 4MB budget, only that sub-table is flushed, producing exactly 1 SST (not 16 SSTs per flush as in the fallback scheme). This is the spec's true intervention for H2 (overlap decided at write admission). Sub-table flushes confirmed: 3034-3037 per run, each producing 1 SST. No corruption errors. Mechanism is correct but performance is poor: 4MB per-subtable budget causes ~3000 flushes over 10M writes (each sub-table gets ~625MB of data / 4MB = ~156 flushes, × 16 = ~2500-3000 total), producing too many small SSTs that overwhelm compaction (209 vs baseline 19 compactions). Stall is severe: 816s median (vs baseline 82s), 268K stall events (vs 51K). Compaction read amplification: 81.2 GB vs baseline 11.8 GB (6.9x increase). Root cause: 4MB per-subtable budget is too small; each flush produces only ~4MB SST, requiring many L0->L1 compaction rounds to keep up. The mechanism achieves overlap reduction (75.8% from baseline) but not enough to meet <=1.2 threshold (median 2.18). The key difference from fallback: fallback produced 16 SSTs per flush (L0 burst), main approach produces 1 SST per flush (no burst) but has 16x more flush events. Both approaches fail but for different reasons: fallback = L0 file count burst (too many files at once), main = flush frequency (too many small flushes).

p_recommend_rationale: P=16 was the spec-mandated partition count. Main approach (PartitionedMemTable write-time routing + independent per-sub-table flush) achieves 75.8% overlap reduction (12.998 -> 2.183 median) but still fails the <=1.2 threshold. The bottleneck is the 4MB per-subtable budget (64MB/16), which causes ~3000 flushes producing small SSTs that overwhelm compaction. Increasing P would further shrink per-subtable budget and worsen the flush frequency problem. Decreasing P (e.g., P=4) would increase per-subtable budget to 16MB, reducing flush count ~4x, but would reduce partitioning effectiveness (overlap would increase). The fundamental tension: more partitions = better overlap reduction but more flush events; fewer partitions = fewer flushes but worse overlap. Neither extreme meets all acceptance criteria simultaneously. Root cause is that per-subtable flush (even at 1 SST/flush) creates too many small SSTs for compaction to handle within the 64MB total memory budget.
measurement_method: Baseline: vanilla RocksDB 11.2.0 (source/rocksdb-exp0-tools/build/db_bench, vanilla engine + zipfian tool-layer flag). Intervention: source/rocksdb-exp1-partition/build/db_bench, branch exp1-partitioned-memtable, commit bdb0615. PartitionedMemTable write-time routing: Put(key) binary-searches L1 key range boundaries to find sub-table id, Add to that sub-table. Each sub-table has 4MB budget (64MB/16). When sub-table fills 4MB, TakeFullSubTable() marks it immutable and schedules a flush for just that sub-table, producing 1 key-range-disjoint L0 SST. WriteBufferManager tracks all 16 sub-tables' total memory (64MB cap). L1 boundaries from VersionStorageInfo::LevelFiles(1); when L1 empty, uniform key space split into P-1 boundaries using 128-bit big-endian arithmetic. WAL write/recovery paths unchanged. Read path unchanged. Compaction strategy unchanged. Auto-compaction enabled (no disable_auto_compactions). Both groups: fillrandom num=20M writes=10M total (1.25M/thread × 8 threads) value=1024 wbs=64MB mwbn=4 tfsb=64MB mblb=256MB level compaction sync=false compression=none seed=42. Metrics: overlap_factor_mean/p99 via overlap_probe (uniform-random 100K sample keys, count L0 files covering each key via GetLiveFilesMetaData); l0_file_count from overlap_probe; compact_read_bytes from rocksdb.compact.read.bytes ticker (--statistics); stall_micros from rocksdb.stall.micros ticker; stall_count from rocksdb.db.write.stall histogram COUNT; write_throughput from db_bench fillrandom ops/sec; compaction_count from rocksdb.compaction.times.micros histogram COUNT; sub_table_flushes from LOG_fillrandom (count of 'flush partition' events). 3 reps for zipfian (median), 1 rep for uniform. overlap_probe runs before readrandom to avoid LOG overwrite; LOG_fillrandom saved before overlap_probe DB open. LD_LIBRARY_PATH=<build_dir>:/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu (no anaconda).
failures_or_na: intervention.overlap_factor_mean=2.18307 > 1.2 threshold (FAIL, but 75.8% reduction from baseline 8.99827)
compaction_read_reduction: baseline 11.8GB -> intervention 81.2GB = +588% INCREASE (FAIL, needs >=40% reduction)
uniform distribution: 1 rep each (not median, due to 10x slower runtime with intervention); zipfian is primary with 3 reps median
uniform intervention overlap=4.68834 (worse than zipfian due to even distribution causing more sub-table contention)

metadata.uniform_reps_note: uniform distribution: 1 rep each (not median, due to ~10x slower runtime vs zipfian); zipfian is primary with 3 reps median
metadata.boundary_strategy: L1 file key range boundaries from VersionStorageInfo::LevelFiles(1); when L1 file count < P-1, uniform key space split using 128-bit big-endian arithmetic over [smallest_user_key, largest_user_key]; hash-based fallback for equal keys

smoke_test.notes: Smoke test confirmed: per-subtable flush mechanism works (each flush produces 1 SST, not 16), no corruption, overlap reduced from baseline.

fallback_scheme_comparison.description: Previous fallback approach (branch exp1-flush-partition): flush-time partition where each flush splits the full memtable into up to 16 SSTs at once.
fallback_scheme_comparison.comparison_notes: Both approaches FAIL all acceptance criteria but for different root causes. Fallback: L0 file count burst (16 SSTs/flush) triggers level0_slowdown_writes stalls. Main approach: per-subtable budget too small (4MB) causes ~3000 flushes, each producing 1 SST, overwhelming compaction with many small SSTs. Main approach has BETTER overlap reduction mechanism (independent flush = no inter-flush overlap) but WORSE throughput due to flush frequency. NOTE: fallback scheme used writes=10M/thread (80M total) vs main scheme writes=10M total (1.25M/thread), so absolute numbers are not directly comparable. Relative comparisons (baseline vs intervention within each scheme) are valid.
